Wise vs Revolut: fees, accounts and who suits whom

By the Ibanora teamPublished November 16, 202610 min read

In short

Wise and Revolut both give you a multi-currency account and a card, and they charge in different ways. As of November 2026, Wise has no plans or subscriptions and adds a fee that varies by currency to the mid-market rate. Revolut sells monthly plans, uses its own exchange rate, and adds a fair usage fee above a monthly exchange limit on its cheaper plans.

The main difference in Wise vs Revolut is how each one charges. As of November 2026, Wise has no plans or subscriptions: you pay a fee each time you convert or send money, on top of the mid-market exchange rate. Revolut has a free Standard plan and several paid plans, uses an exchange rate it sets itself, and adds a fair usage fee once you pass a monthly exchange limit on its cheaper plans. Both give you a multi-currency account with a card. The figures come from each company's UK and US websites; the site for your country may differ.

Wise entries come from Wise's UK pricing page, its help article on currencies, its crypto policy and its business pricing page. Revolut entries come from its UK plans page, UK fees page, UK money transfer page, help article on account details, UK crypto page and UK business plans page. All entries are as of November 2026.

How Wise and Revolut price currency exchange

Wise says on its UK pricing page that it only uses the mid-market rate, "the one you can check on Google". The fee for converting "varies by currency" and starts "From 0.24%" on the UK page and "From 0.23%" on the US page, as of November 2026. Wise also offers "volume discounts when you make big conversions". As a worked example, a 0.24% fee on a £1,000 conversion would be £2.40; the fee for your currency pair may be higher.

Revolut's UK fees page describes a different model, as of November 2026. Within your plan's limit, "You get the Revolut exchange rate" and Revolut adds "an exchange fee (if one applies)". The rate "is set by us" and is variable. The fee is also variable, "depending on the parameters of your exchange (like what you are exchanging and when)". Revolut says it shows the total cost before you exchange where possible. The exception is a card purchase that needs a currency conversion in real time; you see the breakdown in the app afterward.

On top of that sits the fair usage limit. As of November 2026, the UK limits are £1,000 a month on Standard, with a 1% fee on anything above it, and £3,000 on Plus, with a 0.5% fee above it, according to the fees page. A footnote on the plans page gives a combined limit of £1,000 without naming a plan. Premium, Metal and Ultra have no exchange limit. The limit counts currency, crypto and commodities exchanges together. For example, a Standard customer who exchanges £1,500 in a month pays 1% on the £500 above the limit, which is £5, plus any regular exchange fee.

As of November 2026, the US plans page lists exchange limits of $1,000 a month on Standard and $10,000 on Premium, and "Unlimited" on Metal. For Premium it adds: "Fair usage fees may apply after $10,000 within a 30 day period."

Plans and the currencies you can hold

Registering for a Wise account is free, according to its pricing page as of November 2026, and Wise says you "only pay for what you use". Its help centre says: "You can keep 40+ currencies in your account". The same article lists conditions for adding some currencies.

Revolut's UK plans cost nothing for Standard, £3.99 a month for Plus, £8.99 for Premium, £16.99 for Metal and £60 for Ultra, as of November 2026. Paid plans add higher limits, insurance and brand subscriptions. In the US, Revolut lists Standard at $0.00, Premium at $9.99 and Metal at $16.99 a month, and notes that "Plan fees and cancellation fees apply for Premium and Metal plans." Revolut's UK money transfer page says you can "Hold, exchange, and send 36 currencies in-app".

Account details for getting paid

Account details are the bank numbers someone else uses to pay you, such as a UK sort code and account number. Wise's pricing page lists "Getting account details to receive in 22 currencies" as free for personal accounts. Receiving domestic (non-Swift) payments in AUD, CAD, EUR, GBP, HUF, NZD, PHP, SGD and USD is also free. Swift payments cost a fixed fee: 6.11 USD for USD wire and Swift payments, 2.16 GBP for GBP and 2.39 EUR for EUR, as of November 2026. Wise's help article adds that it has "had to stop users from getting PLN account details for now".

Revolut's help article says that, as of November 2026, customers registered in the UK get a GBP sort code and account number, USD details with ACH and wire routing numbers for transfers within the US, a Polish IBAN for transfers within Poland, and SWIFT details "for international transfers in all supported currencies". The article does not list local euro details for UK customers. Revolut's UK fees page charges £8 to add money to a USD local account by Fedwire.

Sending money abroad

The two price cross-border payments differently. As of November 2026:

  • Wise's sending fee "varies by currency" and starts from 0.24% on the UK page. Sending the same currency to another Wise user is free.
  • Wise's card page says you can send "From 32 currencies" "To 104 currencies".
  • On Revolut's Standard plan, transfers to other Revolut users, local payments in your base currency and euro payments within SEPA are free, per its UK fees page.
  • Other international payments on Revolut Standard carry a fee that the app shows before you send. The fees page says this section was updated on 14 October 2026 "with the introduction of fixed fees".
  • Revolut's "Pay All Fees" option charges a flat upfront fee so that intermediary banks' deductions do not reduce what the recipient gets.
  • Revolut's UK money transfer page says you can send to a bank account in "160+ supported countries", and that arrival times depend on the payment method, destination and currency.

Wise vs Revolut for travel: cards and cash

The Wise debit card costs 7 GBP in the UK and 9 USD in the US, with "No subscription fees", as of November 2026. Spending money you already hold in the same currency is free. Wise's card page says the card works "wherever they accept Visa", supports Apple Pay and Google Pay, offers digital cards, and converts automatically when you don't hold the currency.

As of November 2026, Wise's free ATM allowance is 250 GBP a month per account in the UK, then 2.69% of the amount over 250 GBP. In the US it is 250 USD per calendar month, then "1.95 USD + 1.95%" for each withdrawal. ATM operators may add their own fees.

As of November 2026, Revolut's first UK card is free, though a delivery fee applies, and virtual cards are free. Its UK cards page says you can link virtual cards to Apple Pay or Google Pay. On the UK Standard plan you get 5 withdrawals or £200 per rolling month, whichever comes first, then 2% per withdrawal with a minimum of £1. The UK plans page lists a monthly limit of £200 on Plus, £400 on Premium, £800 on Metal and £2,000 on Ultra. In the US, Revolut does not charge its own fee at in-network ATMs. At out-of-network ATMs, Standard pays 2% on every withdrawal, while Premium and Metal can withdraw up to $800 and $1,200 per rolling month before the 2% fee applies. Revolut describes its UK Metal plan as including travel insurance.

Wise vs Revolut for business

Both companies sell a multi-currency business account. Wise's UK business pricing page lists registration as free and a one-time set-up fee of 50 GBP, which covers account details to receive in 22 currencies (account details cost 31 USD on the US page), as of November 2026. Conversion fees start from 0.24%, and Wise says it doesn't "inflate the mid-market exchange rate".

As of November 2026, Revolut Business in the UK has four plans: Basic at £10 a month, Grow from £30, Scale from £90 and a custom Enterprise plan. Basic, Grow and Scale include a monthly amount you can exchange "at the interbank rate": £1,000, £15,000 and £60,000. Above that allowance Revolut charges 0.6%, and 1% for exchanges outside market hours. The monthly transfers without a fee are 10 local and 0 international on Basic, 100 local and 5 international on Grow, and 1,000 local and 25 international on Scale. Outside the allowance, each international transfer costs £5 and each local one £0.20, and other fees apply for SWIFT OUR transfers. The page lists "25+ currencies supported". On the US business plans page, the plans start from $10, $40 and $140 a month.

How each describes its regulatory status

These are each company's own words for its UK and US entities, as of November 2026.

Wise

The footer of Wise's UK site says: "Wise is authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011, Firm Reference 900507, for the issuing of electronic money." Its UK safeguarding article says "Wise Payments Ltd is not a bank" and that its e-money and payment services "are not subject to the Financial Services Compensation Scheme (FSCS)". It says it safeguards customer money by holding "a mix of cash in banks, investments in secure liquid assets (mainly government bonds) and a comparable guarantee".

For the US, Wise's help article says "Wise US Inc. is registered with the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN)" and holds money transmitter licenses in the states it lists. It also says "We are not a bank" and that its transfer service, and balances not opted into its interest feature, are not subject to Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation insurance.

Revolut

Revolut's UK footer says Revolut Bank UK Ltd is "Authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority", and its help centre says "The PRA and the FCA regulate Revolut Bank UK". On protection, the help article says: "If Revolut Bank were to go insolvent, up to £120,000 of eligible deposits in your bank account will be protected by the FSCS." It adds that crypto, commodities and stocks "don't fall under Revolut Bank UK Ltd FSCS protection". A separate company, Revolut Ltd, is described as "authorised by the Financial Conduct Authority to offer e-money and payment services under the Electronic Money Regulations 2011 (FRN: 900562)".

In the US, Revolut's plans page says "Revolut is not a bank". It says banking services for its prepaid card are provided by Lead Bank, and that Revolut Technologies Inc. "is a technology services provider and program manager of the card program".

Crypto and stablecoins

A stablecoin is a crypto token designed to track a currency such as the US dollar. As of November 2026, Wise's crypto policy says "we don't support the purchase, exchange, or trading of cryptocurrencies". You can't send money to exchanges "like Coinbase or Binance" or to crypto wallets. The Wise card is an exception: it can be used anywhere "as long as it's a lawful transaction and supported in the card region", and Wise says this "includes cryptocurrency platforms".

Revolut's UK crypto page lists "300+ tokens" as of November 2026, with fees as low as 0% depending on your plan and trading volume. It says you can move "BTC, ETH, USDC, and 30+ other tokens" between an outside wallet and Revolut, and that fees may apply. Revolut notes that stablecoins carry specific crypto risks, and its footer says Revolut Ltd is registered with the FCA to offer cryptocurrency services. On Standard and Plus, crypto exchanges count toward the monthly fair usage limit.

Which suits whom

Based on each company's pages as of November 2026:

  • You want to pay per transfer rather than a monthly fee: Wise has "no subscriptions or plans", and Revolut's Standard plan is free in the UK and US.
  • You exchange more than £1,000 (UK) or $1,000 (US) a month: Revolut Standard adds a fair usage fee above that limit, and its paid plans raise or remove the limit. Wise's pricing page lists no monthly exchange limit.
  • You withdraw cash abroad: Wise's free allowance is 250 GBP or 250 USD a month, and Revolut's depends on your plan, from £200 to £2,000 a month in the UK.
  • You want deposit protection in the UK: Revolut Bank UK says eligible deposits are protected by the FSCS up to £120,000, and Wise says its UK e-money and payment services are not subject to the FSCS.
  • You want to buy or hold crypto: Wise doesn't support it, and Revolut's UK site lists 300+ tokens.
  • You run a business: Wise's business pricing page lists no plan fee and a one-time set-up fee of 50 GBP, and Revolut Business plans start at £10 a month with allowances that grow with the plan.

Ibanora also has stablecoin wallets alongside its multi-currency accounts. Its accounts and payment services are provided through its partner Mosta Payments Ltd.

Questions

Is Wise or Revolut better for large transfers?

Wise says big conversions get lower prices through volume discounts. On Revolut's UK Standard and Plus plans, exchanges above £1,000 and £3,000 a month carry fair usage fees of 1% and 0.5%, while Premium, Metal and Ultra have no limit, as of November 2026.

Do Wise or Revolut charge more at weekends?

Revolut's UK plans page lists an extra weekend exchange fee of 1% on Standard and 0.5% on Plus, and none on Premium, Metal and Ultra, as of November 2026. In the US, Revolut lists a 1% fee on Standard outside foreign exchange market hours, which it says are all hours except 5:00pm Friday to 6:00pm Sunday Eastern Time. Wise's pricing page does not list a weekend fee.

Can I move money between Wise and Revolut?

Both give UK customers GBP account details. Revolut's UK fees page lists local payments in your base currency as free on Standard, and Wise's pricing page lists receiving domestic GBP payments as free, as of November 2026. Other currencies and Swift payments can carry fees on either side.
